extracted.intended_audience: Princeton communicators and university communications staff (press officers, campus communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for drafting, styling, distributing, and coordinating Princeton University news/press releases for print and online audiences, following AP style with Princeton-specific exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: News releases help make work accessible to everyday people: Inform media of University events and research; Promote Princeton expertise; Reach diverse audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use releases to inform media, showcase Princeton expertise, and reach broad/diverse audiences. Frame content to be accessible to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Princeton Communications support and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: What Princeton Communications helps with: Drafting press releases; Coordinating with academic departments; Identifying experts; Distributing strategically; Following up with media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with Princeton Communications for drafting, expert identification, strategic distribution, and media follow-up to ensure accuracy, consistency, and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses The Associated Press Stylebook for published content, with Princeton-specific exceptions. Apply AP rules for punctuation, capitalization, numbers, dates, titles, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Princeton name usage on first reference
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full institution name on first reference; after first reference, "Princeton" is preferred. This is a Princeton-specific exception to general AP guidance on institutional references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent name usage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After introducing "Princeton University" on first reference, use the shorter form "Princeton" for readability and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty title usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty titles: full title on first reference, last name only after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the full faculty title (e.g., 'Professor of Biology John Smith') on first reference to establish credentials; subsequently refer to individuals by last name only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department name usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Department names: official name on first reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official department or unit name on first reference to ensure institutional accuracy and consistency across communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the University's standard boilerplate language in releases to provide consistent institutional context; also include media contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contacts and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear media contacts and plan for follow-up with reporters as part of the release distribution process to facilitate coverage and questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to general audiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in plain language so non-specialists can understand the significance of research/events; avoid jargon or explain it succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote expertise without overhype
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight Princeton expertise and contributions but avoid exaggerated claims or sensational language; maintain accuracy and measured tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct use of alumni terminology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gender-specific Latin plural forms correctly where relevant (alumni for men/mixed groups, alumnae for women).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of 'the University'
rubrics_metrics.description: "the University" capitalized when referring to Princeton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize "the University" when the phrase specifically refers to Princeton; follow AP/published conventions otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic distribution and media engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributing strategically; Following up with media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan distribution to appropriate outlets and audiences; engage in proactive follow-up (media pitching, answering inquiries) to maximize coverage and ensure accurate reporting.
